summary: Tests cover main requirements (JUnit/JSON parsing, aggregation, flaky detection, markdown output, basic error handling) with clear organization into phases. However, test suite lacks rigor: only happy-path parsing scenarios tested, no malformed XML/JSON tests, no edge cases for test names (special chars, length), empty files, boundary conditions in duration calculations, or exact output format validation. Critical issue: fixture files (junit-ubuntu.xml, junit-windows.xml, results-macos.json, all-passing.json) are referenced but not provided in implementation code, making it impossible to verify test data correctness. Workflow file also not provided. Tests are brittle—they hard-code expected totals (11 tests, 6 passed, 3 failed, 2 skipped) with no way to verify fixtures match. Would catch basic regressions in happy path but miss errors in edge cases and error conditions.
